title: Copilot and Visual Calculations

header.html: Create a narrative visual with Copilot; Use Copilot to create a new report page; Use Copilot to suggest content for a new report page; Create visual calculations by using DAX
the official PL-300 study guide (skills measured as of April 20, 2026)

toc.title: Create report pages and suggest content
Measure, column, visual calculation or calculation group

html:
1What Copilot needs

Copilot in Power BI is an AI assistant that works only with the right capacity and settings. Check the requirements before you check anything else.

Requirement Detail
Capacity A paid Fabric capacity of F2 or higher, or a Premium capacity of P1 or higher
Not enough A trial capacity, or a Pro or PPU license alone
Tenant setting The admin turns on "Users can use Copilot and other features powered by Azure OpenAI"
Region The capacity must be in a supported region
Prompt limit Up to 10,000 characters in one prompt
Delay Copilot can take up to 24 hours to appear after you buy the capacity

Review every Copilot answer. Copilot is generated by AI and can be wrong, so you check the text, the visuals and the measures before you share the report.

Exam tip

. Copilot needs a paid capacity of F2 or higher, or P1 or higher. A trial, Pro alone or PPU alone is not enough. Also remember the tenant setting, a supported region and up to 24 hours of delay.

2Narrative visual with Copilot

A narrative visual with Copilot writes a text summary of what the report shows. When you add the Narrative visual, it opens in Copilot mode.

Item Fact
Scope The whole report, chosen pages or selected visuals
Source It reads the report visuals, not the semantic model directly
Editing Change the text by typing a prompt, such as "make it shorter"
Updating It does not update on its own; the text stays until someone refreshes it
Older mode Smart narrative, with dynamic values (up to 4 per visual and 16 per page)

The scope you choose decides which visuals Copilot reads. A summary of selected visuals describes only those visuals.

Exam tip

. The Copilot narrative reads the report visuals, not the model, and it does not refresh itself. The older smart narrative uses dynamic values that follow the data.

3Create report pages and suggest content

Copilot can build a new report page from the semantic model. In the Power BI service, open the report, choose Edit, then open Copilot.

Path What you do Result
Suggest content for this report Choose that prompt An outline of pages that you can pick from
Describe a page Type what the page should show Copilot builds the page with visuals

After Copilot creates a page, you edit it by asking Copilot to add, change or delete visuals.

Not supported: real-time streaming models, a live connection to Analysis Services, models where implicit measures are disabled, custom visuals, and formatting changes. Copilot builds the content; you still format the page and review it.

Exam tip

. Suggest content gives an outline of pages; describing a page gives one page. Copilot cannot change formatting, and it does not work with a live connection to Analysis Services.

4Visual calculations

A visual calculation is DAX that you write on a visual. It is stored in the visual, not in the model. It refers to the fields already in the visual, so no other visual can use it.

Function What it does
RUNNINGSUM Running total along the axis
MOVINGAVERAGE Average over a moving window of rows
PREVIOUS, NEXT The value of the previous or next row
FIRST, LAST The first or last value on the axis
RANGE, LOOKUP A slice of rows, or a value you look up
COLLAPSE, EXPAND, ISATLEVEL Work at a higher or lower level of the hierarchy

Two arguments steer the functions. Axis sets the direction in the visual, rows or columns. Reset sets where the calculation starts over: NONE, HIGHESTPARENT or LOWESTPARENT.

Total Sales = SUM ( Sales[Amount] )

// Visual calculations, written on a visual that shows Total Sales by Month
Running Sales = RUNNINGSUM ( [Total Sales] )
Moving Average = MOVINGAVERAGE ( [Total Sales], 3 )

Not supported: USERELATIONSHIP, RELATED and RELATEDTABLE; slicer visuals and some AI visuals; pinning to a dashboard; Publish to web; and filtering on the calculation itself.

Exam tip

. A visual calculation lives in the visual, not in the model, and cannot use RELATED or USERELATIONSHIP. It cannot be pinned to a dashboard or published to the web.

5Measure, column, visual calculation or calculation group

Pick the calculation by where it must live and who must reuse it.

You need Use Why
A reusable value that reacts to filters in every visual Measure Calculated at query time in the model; nothing stored
A value per row to slice, sort, group or relate on Calculated column Stored in the model, calculated at refresh, uses memory
A running total, moving average or previous row in one visual Visual calculation Stored in the visual; the model does not change
One set of items, such as year to date, for many measures Calculation group Items use SELECTEDMEASURE; explicit measures only

Creating a calculation group needs the setting Discourage implicit measures turned on.

Exam tip

. Many measures that need the same logic means a calculation group. One visual that needs a running total means a visual calculation. A value to slice by means a calculated column.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A company gives every analyst a Pro license, and its workspaces are on shared capacity. Analysts cannot find Copilot in the report editor. What is required?

  • AA paid Fabric capacity of F2 or higher
  • BA trial Fabric capacity for each workspace
  • CA Premium Per User license for each analyst
  • DA Pro license for each report viewer
Show the answer

Answer: A. Copilot needs a paid Fabric capacity of F2 or higher or a Premium capacity of P1 or higher, and a trial, Pro or PPU alone is not enough.

S2An author adds a Narrative visual with Copilot to a page. A viewer then selects a different region in a slicer. What happens to the narrative text?

  • AIt rewrites itself right away for the new region
  • BIt stays as written until someone refreshes it
  • CIt is removed because the filter changed
  • DIt switches to a smart narrative automatically
Show the answer

Answer: B. The Copilot narrative does not update on its own, so the text stays until it is refreshed.

S3A new report has a semantic model but no pages. The author wants Copilot to propose a set of pages before building any. Which prompt should the author choose?

  • ASummarize the semantic model
  • BSuggest content for this report
  • CCreate a narrative for the report
  • DDescribe a single page in detail
Show the answer

Answer: B. Suggest content for this report returns an outline of pages to pick from, while the others summarize or build one item.

S4An author writes a visual calculation that returns a running total on a column chart. Where is the calculation stored, and who can reuse it?

  • AIn the model, so every visual can reuse it
  • BIn the visual, so no other visual can reuse it
  • CIn the page, so every visual on it can reuse it
  • DIn the table, so only its visuals can reuse it
Show the answer

Answer: B. A visual calculation is stored in the visual and is not part of the model, so other visuals cannot use it.

S5A team needs the same year-to-date and prior-year logic for twelve existing measures without writing twelve copies of each. Which feature should the team use?

  • AA visual calculation on every visual
  • BA calculated column in the Date table
  • CA calculation group with calculation items
  • DA calculated table with a measure for each
Show the answer

Answer: C. A calculation group applies one set of calculation items to many explicit measures through SELECTEDMEASURE.

S6An author uses visual calculations in a report. Which of these actions is not supported?

  • APinning the visual to a dashboard
  • BAdding a moving average to a line chart
  • CComparing each value with the previous one
  • DUsing a running total in a matrix
Show the answer

Answer: A. Visuals that contain a visual calculation cannot be pinned to a dashboard, while running totals, moving averages and previous-row comparisons are supported.

6.2 Recall questions

R1Which capacities allow Copilot?

Show the answer

A paid Fabric capacity of F2 or higher, or a Premium capacity of P1 or higher.

R2What are the prompt limit and the possible delay after you buy the capacity?

Show the answer

10,000 characters, and up to 24 hours.

R3What are the two ways to start a Copilot report page?

Show the answer

Suggest content for this report, or describe the page.

R4What does a Copilot narrative visual read?

Show the answer

The report visuals, not the semantic model directly.

R5Which two arguments control a visual calculation function?

Show the answer

Axis and Reset.

R6What should you do with Copilot output before you share it?

Show the answer

Review it, because it can be wrong.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Requirements Paid F2 or higher, or P1 or higher; not trial, Pro or PPU alone; tenant setting; supported region
Limits 10,000-character prompt; up to 24 hours to appear
Narrative visual Scope: report, pages or visuals; reads report visuals; edit by prompt; does not auto-update
Report page Suggest content gives an outline; describe a page; edit by add, change, delete; no formatting changes
Visual calculation DAX stored in the visual; RUNNINGSUM, MOVINGAVERAGE, PREVIOUS, NEXT; Axis and Reset
Not supported USERELATIONSHIP, RELATED, RELATEDTABLE, slicers, pin to dashboard, Publish to web
Which calculation Measure: reusable; column: per row; visual calculation: one visual; calculation group: many measures
Review Always review Copilot output before sharing
